diameterInterpretation: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 143.77 km effective diameter (catalog ±2.51 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotational phase is illustrative.

calibration.uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
calibration.additionalSystematics: Usui 2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about 10% in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
calibration.diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
calibration.limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Hanuš 2021 TableA.2 reports 316 ASAS-SN observations and both poles(173,-7)/(355,13). Its catalog diameter 128.7 km differs from AKARI143.77 km; neither number is established as this mesh physical volume. The pinned AKARI effective diameter is used only as a stated scale approximation.
